I built the meeting-chat service and steps 1–3 pass, but I couldn't get a real answer out of it: Gemini times out on every call, and meeting-processor isn't running, so step 4 didn't run. I didn't run git, commit, deploy, write A2A code or touch `meeting-processor/`.

**1. py_compile:** no output.

**2. Routes:** your exact command fails here. The installed FastAPI (0.162.0) wraps routers added with `include_router` in an object that has no `.path`, so it raises `AttributeError: '_IncludedRouter' object has no attribute 'path'`. I kept the normal `include_router`, same as meeting-processor, and checked the routes through the OpenAPI schema instead:
```
['/chat', '/chat/{session_id}', '/health']
```

**3. pytest:**
```
tests/test_chat.py::test_chat_response_shape PASSED
tests/test_chat.py::test_chat_reuses_session_id PASSED
tests/test_chat.py::test_delete_unknown_session_returns_404 PASSED
tests/test_health.py::test_health PASSED
========================= 4 passed, 1 warning in 0.31s =========================
```
The one warning comes from Starlette's test client, not this code.

**4. Live test: not done.**
- **meeting-processor:** nothing is listening on port 8000, so I couldn't run the budget question or the Carol follow-up.
- **Gemini:** I started meeting-chat on 8001 and tried a simple two-turn chat that needs no meeting data. Every POST hung until curl gave up after 60s. I then called Gemini directly, without ADK, and `gemini-flash-latest` returned `504 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` twice (after 39s and 59s). Your key works: a different model name came back with a normal "model not available" error rather than an auth failure. So Gemini is slow or failing, not this service. I left the model name as your brief specified.
- **DELETE:** did work live: 204 the first time, 404 when repeated.
- **Not yet proven:** multi-turn memory against the real model is still untested. The tests only check that the route passes the same `session_id` both times.

What I checked in the installed ADK:
- **`event.message`** exists as an alias for `event.content`, so the API in your brief is correct.
- **Async tools:** ADK awaits them.
- **API key:** google-genai only reads `GOOGLE_API_KEY` from the environment, and pydantic-settings doesn't put `.env` values there. `chat_agent.py` copies it across at import.

Choices you may want to change:
- **Reply text:** `chat()` keeps text only from the agent's final response, not every text part, so in-between text sent alongside tool calls doesn't leak into the reply.
- **DELETE:** really deletes the in-memory session (204, or 404 if unknown). All sessions are also lost on restart; both are noted in comments.
- **One shared user:** there's no auth, so every caller is the same ADK user, `"anonymous"`. Anyone who knows a `session_id` can read or delete that conversation; the README says so.
- **Unknown meeting:** `get_meeting` returns `{"error": ...}` instead of raising, so the agent can say so. Any other failure in the agent becomes a 502.
- **No time limit on Gemini calls:** a slow call holds the request open until Gemini itself gives up (about 40–60s above). If you want a cap, it would go in `Agent(generate_content_config=...)`.

To finish step 4, start meeting-processor on 8000, check that Gemini responds again, then run your two curl commands.
